historical_reviews.v3_1: BootOrder is an ordered policy, not merely printable JSON; each reference, uniqueness and ordering rule must be checked against the selected System's valid options.

original_test_intent: Read the selected ComputerSystem's current default BootOrder and validate the ordered option references as a secure read-only configuration snapshot.
original_method: Resolve the intended System member, use trusted curl/jq to GET it once, extract the documented `Boot.BootOrder` array, and validate type, order, uniqueness and membership against the approved BootOptions set.
manual_activity: The platform/security owner supplies a non-source least-privilege secret, trusted TLS, the target System member, firmware Boot schema, allowed BootOption reference set and expected ordering/empty-state policy.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Validated Systems collection and target member
Fresh least-privilege secret provider unrelated to exposed source credentials
Allowed BootOption reference, uniqueness, order and empty-state policy
safety_requirements: Do not execute malformed source syntax
No boot write, one-time boot, reboot, power or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Resolve approved System and valid BootOptions references
Acquire a fresh least-privilege secret safely
Validate array type, order, uniqueness and membership
Archive redacted snapshot and no-write audit
engineer_actions: Replace exposed credential and approve trust method

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The corrected `.Boot.BootOrder` path reflects the intended read, but fixed member identity, `-k`, absent HTTP/schema failure handling and no reference oracle make the YES conclusion unsafe; the Master credential must be treated as exposed.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS and a fresh secret-safe credential, resolve the advertised System member, GET it once, require 2xx JSON and an approved `Boot.BootOrder` array, then validate every ordered unique reference against that System's BootOptions collection.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The single BootOrder read and 15/10 timing remain; no member ID, credential, expected order or permitted reference is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the source password as compromised, use the standard secure Redfish runner, and compare the returned ordered array against a project-owned option/reference policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Repairs malformed syntax and unsafe access, resolves member identity, and changes acceptance from readable output to ordered-reference validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates the current order only; it does not modify, persist or exercise the order and remains separate from SetDefaultBootOrder.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Boot identifiers may disclose topology and may change after firmware or device inventory changes. A syntactically valid array can still be operationally wrong without the approved policy.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent if it preserves certificate/member identity and ordered array evidence. Credential rotation is operational follow-up outside this review, but the exposed literal must never be used. No PATCH/POST or reboot is authorized by this read case.
expected_evidence: Immutable BMC/System identity and firmware Boot schema
Proof a fresh least-privilege credential and trusted certificate path were used without revealing secrets
HTTP status/content type and redacted raw response hash
BootOrder array length, exact ordered redacted references and uniqueness result
Membership comparison to selected System BootOptions
No boot write, reboot, power, firmware or log mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Despite the `BoorOrder` typo and malformed jq, the Master item, System resource and intended BootOrder read are aligned. These are execution defects, not competing source purposes or identities.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read purpose is clear. Secure credentials, target identity, schema and accepted reference policy are concrete owner-supplied prerequisites.

review_improvement: Rejects the exposed credential and malformed/null-prone query, then adds System identity plus ordered BootOption membership validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Boot order is meaningful only as an ordered list of references valid for the selected System. A readable jq result can hide null, duplicate, stale or foreign option IDs, so validation must join the array to that System's BootOptions membership and project order policy. Because the Master embeds a root password, that literal is compromised by definition and cannot be reused even in an isolated lab; a separately provisioned least-privilege secret is mandatory.
